findings.title: `fixes_added` compares against a judged version that never holds a fix task
quotes: at the tasks gate, the IDs of tasks under `#### Fixes` in the current `tasks.md` that the judged version doesn't hold; `[]` at every other gate.
A file as its gate judges it: tasks.md without its `#### Fixes` sections, any other file as it is.
text = lambda p: planned(p.name, p.read_text()) if gate == "tasks" else p.read_text()
Given a tasks gate where nothing was added under `#### Fixes` since the last round, when `nio jury fixcheck` and `nio jury changed` run, then their output is the same as before this change.
findings.fix: Have CT-4 say where the fix tasks present at the judged round come from. One option is for `collect` to record the fix task IDs it saw in the ledger next to the version, and have `fixes_added` subtract those. Add a TC where a fix task predates the last round and must not be listed.

sources.situation: In the existing code, `collect` stores `blob(root, text, write)` with `text = artefact(root, slug, gate)`. At the tasks gate, `artefact` passes `tasks.md` through `planned()`, which removes every `#### Fixes` section. So the judged version (`led["versions"]`, which `diff` reads back) never contains a fix task. CT-4 defines added fix tasks as those "the judged version doesn't hold", which means every fix task in `tasks.md`, including ones added before the last round. Once one fix task exists from an earlier round, AC-11's "nothing was added since the last round" case changes both the pack and the `changed` output. TC-11 doesn't catch this because its setup ("as TC-8 without T-30") has no fix tasks at all.

findings.reason: `artefact()` runs `tasks.md` through `planned()` at the tasks gate (jury.py:187-191), and `collect` stores that text as the judged version, so the judged version never holds a fix task. CT-4's "that the judged version doesn't hold" therefore lists every fix task in `tasks.md`, including ones added in earlier rounds, which contradicts AC-11. TC-11's setup has no fix task, so it can't catch this.
findings.note: CT-4: collect records the Fixes IDs present at each round (led fixes); fixes_added subtracts the last round's; TC-11 now has a fix task that predates the round and must not be listed.

findings.title: The added fix task is kept out of `changed`'s list, though the ACs put it there
quotes: prints, after its four lines, `added under Fixes: <T-n, ...>` when `fixes_added` is non-empty; nothing more otherwise.
Observable: T-30 is in the changed list; the lenses-to-re-run list is empty.
Assert: changed IDs `[]`, lenses to re-run `[]`, `fixes_added` `["T-30"]`.
findings.fix: Either state in CT-6 that the `added under Fixes:` line is the changed list FR-7 means, and reword TC-20's assertion to match, or add T-30 to the `changed:` line without adding any lens to re-run.

sources.situation: Today the CLI prints `changed: <ids>` from `jury.changed`. AC-9 says T-30 is "among the changed IDs it reports", and AC-24 says T-30 "is in the changed list". The plan instead keeps `changed:` free of T-30 and prints it on a separate fifth line. TC-20 then asserts the changed IDs are `[]`, which reads as the opposite of AC-24's observable.

findings.note: CT-6 states the 'added under Fixes:' line is FR-7's list; TC-20's assert reworded to match.

findings.title: CT-11 copies `tasks.md` to a run folder the tasks skill never creates
quotes: step 3 copies `tasks.md` to the run folder before the evaluator
3. **Rate.** Run the `nio-evaluator` subagent on `tasks.md`. It sets every `Tier:` (with a reason) and `Effort:`.
findings.fix: Name the path in CT-11, for example `.nio/runs/<run>/tasks.before.md` after `nio run <slug>`, or a scratch path outside `.nio/specs/<slug>/`, and have step 3 say the same.

sources.situation: `skills/tasks/SKILL.md` never starts a run (`nio run`) or names a run folder, so "the run folder" points at nothing in the skill. The agent following step 3 has to guess where the copy goes. A copy under `.nio/specs/<slug>/` would land among the effort's own files.

findings.note: CT-11: step 3 runs nio run and copies to .nio/runs/<run>/tasks.before.md.

findings.title: `--rated-from`'s relation to the existing `nio check tasks` run and output is unstated
quotes: Returns: exit 0 when every differing line pair is a `- Tier:`, `- Effort:` or `- Mode:` line and none reads `to be rated`.
print("\n".join([f"ERROR {e}" for e in errors] + notes + [f"{len(errors)} errors"]))
findings.fix: State in CT-7 that `--rated-from` adds `rated_from`'s errors to `tasks.check`'s, printed through the existing `ERROR …`/`N errors` output, or that it replaces the normal check. Make TC-22/TC-23 assert that choice.

sources.situation: The existing `nio check tasks` branch in `cli.main` always runs `tasks.check` and prints `ERROR …` lines, the estimate and an `N errors` total. CT-7 says it is like `tasks.check`, but its exit-0 rule depends only on the rating diff. Its error format (`<path>:<line>: not a rating line: …`) also has no `ERROR` prefix. The plan doesn't say whether `--rated-from` skips the normal checks or adds to them. It also doesn't say whether its errors go through the same `ERROR`/count output that skills already read.

findings.note: CT-7: --rated-from adds its errors to tasks.check's, printed as ERROR lines with the N errors total; TC-22 asserts it.

findings.title: TC-6 passes on today's code: its fixture never gives TC-6 and TC-7 a file
quotes: a test file `tests/test_c.py` failing on `assert False`.
if named and not any(f in command for f in named):
findings.fix: In TC-6's setup, give the fixture tests.md TC-6 and TC-7 entries whose `File:` lines name files other than `tests/test_c.py` (for example `tests/test_e.py`), so today's code refuses and only the own-ID change passes.

sources.situation: `test_files` keeps only IDs that have an entry in tests.md (`if t in tcs`). TC-6's setup defines no `### TC-6` or `### TC-7` entries with `File:` lines. With no entries, `named` is empty today, red runs the command and accepts it. TC-6 passes before any work, and it still passes if `own` is never wired into `test_files`. AC-6 matches the T-2 defect that motivated US-2, so the bug this story fixes gets through.

findings.reason: `test_files` keeps only TC IDs that have an entry in tests.md (implement.py:349, `if t in tcs`). TC-6's setup defines no TC-6 or TC-7 entries, so `named` is empty and `red` (implement.py:441) runs the command and accepts it. TC-6 passes on today's code and never exercises `own`.
findings.note: TC-6: tests.md defines TC-6 and TC-7 with File tests/test_e.py, so today's code refuses.

findings.title: TC-13 and TC-30 can pass without stripping NIO_PERF
quotes: `NIO_PERF=1` in the test process's environment; T-1 at green.
if not reasons and epic_closes:
The first claim's start of the stage (CT-5, FR-16, FR-20, FR-35, FR-36, FR-46): onto `nio/<slug>`, then the
findings.fix: State that T-1 is the only task of its epic, so the review runs the suite. Write the baseline line from a run without `NIO_PERF`, or with a `failing` list that excludes the test. Add a control assert: with today's `run`, that is with the env passed through, the review fails.

sources.situation: `review` runs the suite only when the task closes its epic, and the setup doesn't say T-1 does. The baseline is taken at the first claim by the same `run`. If that happens in the test process with `NIO_PERF=1` set, the NIO_PERF-sensitive test is already failing at baseline. The review then counts it as `still`, not new, and passes. Either way "the review passes; T-1's attempt count is unchanged" holds on today's code, where `run` doesn't strip `NIO_PERF`.

findings.reason: The baseline comes from the same `run` (implement.py:15-27, which passes the environment through) via `suite`. With `NIO_PERF=1` in the test process, the NIO_PERF-sensitive test is already failing at baseline. `review` (implement.py:493-494) then counts it as `still`, not new, so TC-13 and TC-30 pass without the fix. The setup also doesn't say T-1 closes its epic, and `review` runs the suite only when it does (implement.py:483).
findings.note: TC-13: T-1 is its epic's only task; claimed with NIO_PERF unset so the baseline passes, then NIO_PERF=1 before green.

findings.title: TC-14's failing test exists at baseline, so the review counts it as old and passes
quotes: Setup: as TC-13, with the suite's test failing on `assert 1 == 2` whatever the environment.
Given a task whose change breaks a test's assertion
findings.fix: Take the baseline with the test passing. Then, as T-1's change after the claim, edit the test or the code so it fails on `assert 1 == 2`, with T-1 closing its epic.

sources.situation: AC-15 is about a failure the task's change introduces. The setup has a test that fails in every environment from the start. The baseline therefore records it as failing, and `review` puts it in `still`, not in `new failures`. A correct implementation would let this review pass, so the assert "the review fails naming the failing test, and uses one attempt" fails for a reason unrelated to the AC. A bug such as `run` dropping the whole environment instead of only `NIO_PERF` would not be the thing this test checks.

findings.reason: TC-14's test fails on `assert 1 == 2` in every environment, so the baseline records it as failing. `review` classes it as `still` (implement.py:494), not under "new failures" (implement.py:495-496), so a correct implementation passes the review. That contradicts the assert "the review fails naming the failing test" and AC-15's "a failure the task's change introduces".
findings.note: TC-14: the test passes at baseline and T-1's change makes it fail; T-1 closes its epic.

findings.title: TC-15's "20 output lines checked" can't be observed through status_speed's contract
quotes: the first returns with 20 output lines checked
Shape: `status_speed(clock=time.perf_counter)`
findings.fix: Either have `status_speed` return the output it checked and assert it has 20 lines, or add a case where status yields fewer lines (or a non-zero code) with `NIO_PERF` unset and assert it raises.

sources.situation: CT-10 gives `status_speed` no return value. "Returns with 20 output lines checked" can therefore only mean "didn't raise". One bug would get through: an early return when `NIO_PERF` is unset that skips the `code == 0 and len(out.splitlines()) == 20` check. FR-15 requires that check without `NIO_PERF`.

findings.note: CT-10: status_speed returns the output; TC-15 asserts 20 lines and adds a 19-line case that raises.
